rules.title: New Jersey Law Against Discrimination (LAD) – source of lawful income
rules.requirement: Landlords may not discriminate in housing based on the source of lawful income or source of lawful rent or mortgage payment, so a landlord cannot deny a Section 8 voucher holder an apartment solely because of that income source.
rules.penalty: Complaint to the Division on Civil Rights within 180 days (free), or suit in NJ Superior Court within two years; the document states no specific penalty amounts.
rules.status_basis: Described as existing law enforced by the Division on Civil Rights.

exempt_if.text: rental of a single apartment or flat in a two-family dwelling, the other occupancy unit of which is occupied by the owner as his/her residence

exempt_if.name: owner_occupied
exempt_if.text: other unit occupied by the owner as his/her residence at the time of rental
rental of a room or rooms in a one-family dwelling

exempt_if.name: owner_occupied
exempt_if.text: one-family dwelling occupied by the owner or occupant as his/her residence at the time of rental

coverage.summary: Applies to the sale or rental of all property, business or residential.
coverage.exemptions_summary: Exempts renting one unit of an owner-occupied two-family dwelling and renting rooms in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling.

rules.quoted_span: This means, for example, that a landlord cannot deny the lawful recipient of a Section 8 HUD voucher the right to rent an apartment based solely on that source of lawful income.
